findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. They could repeat it after one read.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The next step is linked near the top, and the Next steps section gives a concrete path: prerequisites, clone, `./setup.sh`, then `athena ask "add a changelog"`. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: This is the root URL of Athena's site, but the title and almost all of the body are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets three intro paragraphs, then a long state machine for a tool they may never have heard of.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / h1 "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The page is offered as a demonstration, but it never shows the features the intro promises. There is no model, cost or verdict for this study, so a newcomer sees claims and citations but no evidence of the accountability that is meant to set Athena apart.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: A link for the owner sits in the header of a public page. To a newcomer, "your decision" reads as addressed to them and is confusing.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Several terms are defined twice, in full, word for word: in scope, red, green, captain, yolo and home. Statements such as the capacity and reopen rules also repeat across Start here, the transition cards and the design cards. All this repetition makes an already dense page longer.
findings.source: Words used first / Glossary: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: This section and the Limits note "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths" describe Athena's internal process. They mean nothing to a newcomer and do not help them act.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The page never says which repository the command acts on (presumably the current directory) or whether an API key or paid account is needed beyond Claude Code. A newcomer may hesitate before running it.
findings.source: Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog". It shows how it read the request and its predictions; press Enter to run it on your repository.

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim to file and line links at a pinned commit. A newcomer can check any statement, which backs up the intro's promise of traceability.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.
